verses.text: तपःस्वाध्यायनिरतं तपस्वी वाग्विदां वरम् । नारदं परिपप्रच्छ वाल्मीकिर्मुनिपुंगवम् ॥
verses.english: The ascetic Vālmīki asked Nārada, devoted to austerity and Vedic study, best of those who know speech, bull among sages.
verses.gold_issues: DCS lemma of निरतम् given as निरम् (correct root नि+रम्); acceptable.

verses.text: को न्वस्मिन्साम्प्रतं लोके गुणवान्कश्च वीर्यवान् । धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च सत्यवाक्यो दृढव्रतः ॥
verses.english: Who now in this world is endowed with virtues, and who [is] valorous, knowing dharma, grateful, truthful in speech, firm in his vows?
verses.gold_issues: verbless questions; the epithets of line 2 are taken as predicates of the second कः. कृतज्ञ kept unsplit by DCS (lexicalised).

verses.text: चारित्रेण च को युक्तः सर्वभूतेषु को हितः । विद्वान्कः कः समर्थश्च कश्चैकप्रियदर्शनः ॥
verses.english: And who is endowed with good conduct, who is beneficial to all beings? Who is learned, who is capable, and who is uniquely pleasing to behold?
verses.gold_issues: adjectival participles (युक्त) in verbless questions treated as विधेय, not क्रिया.

verses.text: आत्मवान्को जितक्रोधो मतिमान्को ऽनसूयकः । कस्य बिभ्यति देवाश्च जातरोषस्य संयुगे ॥
verses.english: Who is self-possessed, who has conquered anger? Who is wise, who is free from envy? Of whom, when his wrath is roused in battle, are even the gods afraid?
verses.gold_issues: कस्य = genitive of the feared one with भी (अपादान sense, 1.4.25 भीत्रार्थानां भयहेतुः); च after देवाः read as "even".

verses.text: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं परं कौतूहलं हि मे । महर्षे त्वं समर्थो ऽसि ज्ञातुमेवंविधं नरम् ॥
verses.english: I wish to hear this, for great is my curiosity; great sage, you are able to know such a man.
verses.gold_issues: परं कौतूहलं हि मे is a verbless existential clause ("there is great curiosity in me"); कौतूहलम् taken as its subject, परम् attributive. DCS tags परम् PRON; it is an adjective here.

verses.text: श्रुत्वा चैतत्त्रिलोकज्ञो वाल्मीकेर्नारदो वचः । श्रूयतामिति चामन्त्र्य प्रहृष्टो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
verses.english: And Nārada, knower of the three worlds, having heard this speech of Vālmīki and having addressed [him with] "Let it be heard," delighted, spoke [these] words.
verses.gold_issues: quoted श्रूयताम् treated as a subordinate clause headed by आमन्त्र्य; त्रिलोक (itself a द्विगु) kept unsplit by DCS.

verses.text: बहवो दुर्लभाश्चैव ये त्वया कीर्तिता गुणाः । मुने वक्ष्याम्यहं बुद्ध्वा तैर्युक्तः श्रूयतां नरः ॥
verses.english: The qualities which you have proclaimed, many and indeed hard to find – O sage, having reflected, I shall tell [them]: let the man endowed with them be heard [of].
verses.gold_issues: relative clause ये…कीर्तिताः attached to its correlative तैः.

verses.text: इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवो रामो नाम जनैः श्रुतः । नियतात्मा महावीर्यो द्युतिमान्धृतिमान्वशी ॥

compounds.vigraha: इक्ष्वाकूणां वंशः इक्ष्वाकुवंशः, सः प्रभवः यस्य सः

verses.english: [One] sprung from the Ikṣvāku line, Rāma by name, self-controlled, of great valour, radiant, resolute, master of himself, is heard of by people.
verses.gold_issues: श्रुतः is a क्त predicate; रामः = कर्म (nominative with passive), जनैः = कर्ता.

verses.text: बुद्धिमान्नीतिमान्वाग्मी श्रीमाञ्शत्रुनिबर्हणः । विपुलांसो महाबाहुः कम्बुग्रीवो महाहनुः ॥
verses.english: [He is] intelligent, versed in statecraft, eloquent, glorious, destroyer of enemies, broad-shouldered, mighty-armed, with a neck [shaped] like a conch, with a large jaw.
verses.gold_issues: epithets of the understood Rāma (subject in verse 8). DCS lemma ग्रीव for the final member (stem ग्रीवा shortened in the बहुव्रीहि) – acceptable.

verses.text: महोरस्को महेष्वासो गूढजत्रुररिंदमः । आजानुबाहुः सुशिराः सुललाटः सुविक्रमः ॥
verses.english: [He is] broad-chested, a great bowman, with collarbones concealed [in flesh], a subduer of foes, with arms reaching to the knees, with a fine head, a fine forehead and a fine stride.
verses.gold_issues: DCS lists आजानु and सु as separate ADV words, but आजानुबाहुः, सुशिराः, सुललाटः, सुविक्रमः are single बहुव्रीहि compounds; treated here as compound members (समासपूर्वपद). DCS form शिरास् = सुशिराः (बहुव्रीहि of शिरस्). अरिंदम kept unsplit (उपपद compound).

verses.text: समः समविभक्ताङ्गः स्निग्धवर्णः प्रतापवान् । पीनवक्षा विशालाक्षो लक्ष्मीवाञ्शुभलक्षणः ॥
verses.english: [He is] well-proportioned, with evenly-formed limbs, of glossy complexion, majestic, full-chested, large-eyed, endowed with splendour, bearing auspicious marks.
verses.gold_issues: epithets of the understood Rāma. DCS tags सम as PRON (it is an adjective here). अक्ष = अक्षि with समासान्त षच् (5.4.113).

verses.text: धर्मज्ञः सत्यसंधश्च प्रजानां च हिते रतः । यशस्वी ज्ञानसम्पन्नः शुचिर्वश्यः समाधिमान् ॥
verses.english: [He is] a knower of dharma, true to his promise, and devoted to the welfare of the subjects, renowned, rich in knowledge, pure, disciplined, possessed of concentration.
verses.gold_issues: epithets of the understood Rāma; adjectival participles (रत, सम्पन्न) treated as विधेय.

verses.text: रक्षिता जीवलोकस्य धर्मस्य परिरक्षिता । वेदवेदाङ्गतत्त्वज्ञो धनुर्वेदे च निष्ठितः ॥

compounds.vigraha: वेदाश्च वेदाङ्गानि च वेदवेदाङ्गानि, तेषां तत्त्वं जानाति इति

verses.english: [He is] the protector of the world of living beings, the guardian of dharma, a knower of the true essence of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, and well-grounded in the science of archery.
verses.gold_issues: जीवलोकस्य, धर्मस्य are genitive objects of the agent nouns रक्षिता/परिरक्षिता (कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति, 2.3.65), marked सम्बन्ध. जीवलोक, वेदाङ्ग, धनुर्वेद kept unsplit by DCS.

verses.text: सर्वशास्त्रार्थतत्त्वज्ञः स्मृतिमान्प्रतिभानवान् । सर्वलोकप्रियः साधुरदीनात्मा विचक्षणः ॥

compounds.vigraha: सर्वाणि शास्त्राणि, तेषाम् अर्थानां तत्त्वं जानाति इति
न दीनः अदीनः, अदीनः आत्मा यस्य सः

verses.english: [He is] a knower of the true meaning of all the treatises, possessed of good memory, quick-witted, beloved of all the world, virtuous, of undejected spirit, discerning.
verses.gold_issues: DCS splits the negative prefix अ of अदीनात्मा as a separate PART; treated as a compound member.

verses.text: सर्वदाभिगतः सद्भिः समुद्र इव सिन्धुभिः । आर्यः सर्वसमश्चैव सदैकप्रियदर्शनः ॥
verses.english: [He is] always approached by the good, as the ocean [is approached] by rivers; noble, impartial towards all indeed, ever uniquely pleasing to behold.
verses.gold_issues: simile with shared participle: समुद्रः/सिन्धुभिः take the roles they would have with अभिगतः (nominative patient = कर्म, instrumental agent = कर्ता). सर्वसम could also be "equal to all"; read "even-minded towards all".

verses.text: स च सर्वगुणोपेतः कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः । समुद्र इव गाम्भीर्ये धैर्येण हिमवानिव ॥
verses.english: And he, endowed with all virtues, increaser of Kausalyā's joy, [is] like the ocean in depth, like the Himālaya in steadfastness.
verses.gold_issues: DCS gives the form हिमवन्त् (a stem); the pada is हिमवान्.

verses.text: विष्णुना सदृशो वीर्ये सोमवत्प्रियदर्शनः । कालाग्निसदृशः क्रोधे क्षमया पृथिवीसमः ॥

compounds.vigraha: कालः एव अग्निः कालाग्निः, तेन सदृशः

verses.english: [He is] equal to Viṣṇu in valour, pleasing to behold like the moon, like the fire of time (universal destruction) in anger, equal to the earth in patience.
verses.gold_issues: DCS splits सोमवत् into सोम (compound member) + वत् (ADV); वत् is a taddhita suffix, not a compound member – kept as given, type अज्ञात.

verses.text: धनदेन समस्त्यागे सत्ये धर्म इवापरः । तमेवंगुणसम्पन्नं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम् ॥
verses.english: [He is] equal to Kubera in generosity, in truthfulness like a second Dharma. That Rāma, endowed with such virtues, of true valour – [Daśaratha wished to unite him with the office of crown prince, verse 19].
verses.gold_issues: रामम् and its qualifiers are the object of संयोक्तुम् in verse 19 (head - within this verse). DCS splits एवं off एवंगुणसम्पन्नम् as a separate ADV; treated as compound member. धनद = Kubera.

verses.text: ज्येष्ठं श्रेष्ठगुणैर्युक्तं प्रियं दशरथः सुतम् । यौवराज्येन संयोक्तुमैच्छत्प्रीत्या महीपतिः ॥
verses.english: King Daśaratha, out of affection, wished to unite [his] eldest son, endowed with excellent qualities, beloved, with the office of crown prince.
verses.gold_issues: प्रीत्या = instrumental of cause (हेतौ). महीपति kept unsplit by DCS.

verses.text: तस्याभिषेकसम्भारान्दृष्ट्वा भार्याथ कैकयी । पूर्वं दत्तवरा देवी वरमेनमयाचत । विवासनं च रामस्य भरतस्याभिषेचनम् ॥
verses.english: Then [his] wife, queen Kaikeyī, to whom a boon had been granted earlier, having seen the preparations for his consecration, asked for this boon: the banishment of Rāma and the consecration of Bharata.
verses.gold_issues: विवासनम्/अभिषेचनम् are appositions to वरम् (different gender), marked विशेषण; रामस्य/भरतस्य are genitive objects of verbal nouns (सम्बन्ध). पूर्वम् qualifies दत्त- inside the compound. DCS lemma कैकयी here vs कैकेयी in verse 22 (variant spelling). Verse has three lines.

verses.text: स सत्यवचनाद्राजा धर्मपाशेन संयतः । विवासयामास सुतं रामं दशरथः प्रियम् ॥
verses.english: That king Daśaratha, bound by the noose of dharma, because of his truthful word banished his beloved son Rāma.
verses.gold_issues: सत्यवचनात् = ablative of cause (हेतु), marked अपादान. धर्मपाश is a रूपक-कर्मधारय.

verses.text: स जगाम वनं वीरः प्रतिज्ञामनुपालयन् । पितुर्वचननिर्देशात्कैकेय्याः प्रियकारणात् ॥
verses.english: That hero, keeping his promise, went to the forest because of the command of his father's word and for the sake of pleasing Kaikeyī.
verses.gold_issues: ablatives of cause marked अपादान; गम् takes the destination in the accusative (कर्म).

verses.text: तं व्रजन्तं प्रियो भ्राता लक्ष्मणो ऽनुजगाम ह । स्नेहाद्विनयसम्पन्नः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः ॥
verses.english: [His] beloved brother Lakṣmaṇa, endowed with modesty, increaser of Sumitrā's joy, out of affection indeed followed him as he went.
verses.gold_issues: स्नेहात् = ablative of cause.

verses.text: सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्ना नारीणामुत्तमा वधूः । सीताप्यनुगता रामं शशिनं रोहिणी यथा ॥
verses.english: Sītā too, the bride, best among women, endowed with all auspicious marks, followed Rāma, as Rohiṇī [follows] the moon.
verses.gold_issues: अनुगता = कर्तरि क्त of a verb of motion (3.4.72), so सीता = कर्ता, रामम् = कर्म. Simile with shared verb: शशिनम्/रोहिणी take the roles they would have with अनुगता. नारीणाम् = निर्धारण genitive.

verses.text: पौरैरनुगतो दूरं पित्रा दशरथेन च । शृङ्गवेरपुरे सूतं गङ्गाकूले व्यसर्जयत् ॥
verses.english: Followed far by the citizens and by [his] father Daśaratha, [Rāma] dismissed the charioteer at Śṛṅgaverapura on the bank of the Gaṅgā.
verses.gold_issues: अनुगतः (passive क्त) qualifies the unexpressed subject of व्यसर्जयत्; marked विधेय>verb as no subject word exists. दूरम् is an adverbial accusative (DCS: ADJ Acc), marked अव्यय.

verses.text: ते वनेन वनं गत्वा नदीस्तीर्त्वा बहूदकाः । चित्रकूटमनुप्राप्य भरद्वाजस्य शासनात् ॥
verses.english: They, having gone from forest to forest, having crossed rivers with abundant water, having reached Citrakūṭa at the instruction of Bharadvāja – [lived there happily, verse 27].
verses.gold_issues: no finite verb in this verse; the absolutives share the agent of न्यवसन् (verse 27), so the last absolutive takes head - here. वनेन = instrumental of route ("through forest after forest"). शासनात् = ablative of cause.

verses.text: रम्यमावसथं कृत्वा रममाणा वने त्रयः । देवगन्धर्वसंकाशास्तत्र ते न्यवसन्सुखम् ॥
verses.english: Having made a lovely dwelling, those three, delighting in the forest, resembling gods and gandharvas, lived there happily.
verses.gold_issues: सुखम् adverbial (DCS ADV), marked अव्यय.

verses.text: चित्रकूटं गते रामे पुत्रशोकातुरस्तदा । राजा दशरथः स्वर्गं जगाम विलपन्सुतम् ॥
verses.english: When Rāma had gone to Citrakūṭa, King Daśaratha, afflicted by grief for his son, lamenting [his] son, then went to heaven.
verses.gold_issues: चित्रकूटं गते रामे = सति सप्तमी (locative absolute); चित्रकूटम् = goal of गत (कर्म).

verses.text: मृते तु तस्मिन्भरतो वसिष्ठप्रमुखैर्द्विजैः । नियुज्यमानो राज्याय नैच्छद्राज्यं महाबलः । स जगाम वनं वीरो रामपादप्रसादकः ॥
verses.english: But when he had died, mighty Bharata, being appointed to the kingship by the brahmins headed by Vasiṣṭha, did not want the kingdom; that hero went to the forest, seeking to win the favour of Rāma's feet.
verses.gold_issues: मृते तस्मिन् = सति सप्तमी. द्विजैः = agent of the passive participle नियुज्यमानः. राज्याय = dative of purpose. Verse has three lines and two main clauses.

verses.text: पादुके चास्य राज्याय न्यासं दत्त्वा पुनः पुनः । निवर्तयामास ततो भरतं भरताग्रजः ॥
verses.english: And then Bharata's elder brother, having given his sandals as a pledge for the kingdom, made Bharata turn back, again and again [urging him].
verses.gold_issues: अस्य read as "his (Rāma's)" sandals; it could also be a genitive for dative ("to him"). न्यासम् is a predicative apposition to पादुके (different number), marked विशेषण. DCS keeps भरताग्रज unsplit (भरतस्य अग्रजः).

verses.text: स काममनवाप्यैव रामपादावुपस्पृशन् । नन्दिग्रामे ऽकरोद्राज्यं रामागमनकाङ्क्षया ॥
verses.english: He, not having obtained his wish at all, touching Rāma's feet, exercised the kingship at Nandigrāma, out of longing for Rāma's return.
verses.gold_issues: DCS splits the negative अन् of अनवाप्य as a separate PART while अवाप्य is not a compound member; kept as अव्यय negating the absolutive. काङ्क्षया = instrumental of cause.

verses.text: रामस्तु पुनरालक्ष्य नागरस्य जनस्य च । तत्रागमनमेकाग्रे दण्डकान्प्रविवेश ह ॥
verses.english: But Rāma, foreseeing again the coming there of the townsfolk and the [country] people, with a concentrated mind entered the Daṇḍaka [forests].
verses.gold_issues: the text reads एकाग्रे (DCS: Loc Masc Sing); other editions have एकाग्रः qualifying रामः. Taken as an adverbial locative of manner; the masculine gender is doubtful. नागरस्य जनस्य च could also be one phrase "of the city people".

verses.text: विराधं राक्षसं हत्वा शरभङ्गं ददर्श ह । सुतीक्ष्णं चाप्यगस्त्यं च अगस्त्यभ्रातरं तथा ॥
verses.english: Having slain the rākṣasa Virādha, [he] saw Śarabhaṅga, and also Sutīkṣṇa, and Agastya, and likewise Agastya's brother.
verses.gold_issues: DCS tags अगस्त्यम् as Nom Neut; it is Acc Masc (object of ददर्श). Subject (Rāma) unexpressed.

verses.text: अगस्त्यवचनाच्चैव जग्राहैन्द्रं शरासनम् । खड्गं च परमप्रीतस्तूणी चाक्षयसायकौ ॥
verses.english: And at Agastya's word indeed, [he], greatly pleased, took the bow of Indra, and a sword, and two quivers with inexhaustible arrows.
verses.gold_issues: परमप्रीतः qualifies the unexpressed subject (marked विधेय>verb, as in verse 25). DCS lemma तूणि for तूणी (dual of तूण/तूणी); शरासन tagged Masc (usually Neut).

verses.text: वसतस्तस्य रामस्य वने वनचरैः सह । ऋषयो ऽभ्यागमन्सर्वे वधायासुररक्षसाम् ॥
verses.english: While that Rāma was dwelling in the forest with the forest-dwellers, all the sages came [to him] for the slaying of the asuras and rākṣasas.
verses.gold_issues: वसतस्तस्य रामस्य = genitive absolute (convention added: both words सम्बन्ध, participle heads its noun and depends on the main verb); it may also be read as the genitive of the person approached. रक्षसाम् = genitive object of the verbal noun वध.

verses.text: तेन तत्रैव वसता जनस्थाननिवासिनी । विरूपिता शूर्पणखा राक्षसी कामरूपिणी ॥
verses.english: By him, dwelling right there, Śūrpaṇakhā, the rākṣasī living in Janasthāna, able to take any form at will, was disfigured.
verses.gold_issues: विरूपिता is a passive क्त predicate: तेन = कर्ता, शूर्पणखा = कर्म. कामरूपिन् kept unsplit by DCS.

verses.text: ततः शूर्पणखावाक्यादुद्युक्तान्सर्वराक्षसान् । खरं त्रिशिरसं चैव दूषणं चैव राक्षसम् ॥
verses.english: Then all the rākṣasas, roused by Śūrpaṇakhā's words, Khara and Triśiras, and also the rākṣasa Dūṣaṇa – [Rāma slew in battle, verse 38].
verses.gold_issues: no verb; all accusatives are objects of निजघान (verse 38). The first object takes head - and the coordinated objects depend on it. त्रिशिरस् kept unsplit.

verses.text: निजघान रणे रामस्तेषां चैव पदानुगान् । रक्षसां निहतान्यासन्सहस्राणि चतुर्दश ॥
verses.english: Rāma slew [them] in battle, and also their followers; fourteen thousand of the rākṣasas were slain.
verses.gold_issues: पदानुग kept unsplit (पदम् अनुगच्छति इति, उपपद-तत्पुरुष). DCS gives चतुर्दश Number=Sing; as a numeral adjective of सहस्राणि it is plural.

verses.text: ततो ज्ञातिवधं श्रुत्वा रावणः क्रोधमूर्छितः । सहायं वरयामास मारीचं नाम राक्षसम् ॥
verses.english: Then, having heard of the slaughter of his kinsmen, Rāvaṇa, swooning with rage, chose as [his] ally a rākṣasa named Mārīca.
verses.gold_issues: सहायम् is a predicative accusative ("as ally") with वरयामास, marked विशेषण of मारीचम्.

verses.text: वार्यमाणः सुबहुशो मारीचेन स रावणः । न विरोधो बलवता क्षमो रावण तेन ते ॥
verses.english: That Rāvaṇa, being restrained very often by Mārīca [– verse 41]: "Rāvaṇa, hostility with that mighty one is not proper for you."
verses.gold_issues: रावणः's verb is in verse 41; line 2 is Mārīca's direct speech (verbless; विरोधः subject, क्षमः predicate). DCS form रावणैस् is wrong: the vocative is रावण. DCS gives तेन Neut; it is Masc agreeing with बलवता. DCS splits सु off सुबहुशः; kept as अव्यय. ते could also be genitive.
